new_candidates.body:
## Summary
With lerobot 0.7.0, evaluating a language-conditioned policy (SmolVLA) on `aloha` sends the gym
id (`"AlohaTransferCube-v0"`) as `task` / `task_description`. The policy was trained on the
dataset's instruction ("Pick up the cube with the right arm and transfer it to the left arm."), so
it is conditioned on a meaningless prompt and looks completely broken. PushT does the same: its
env reports `"PushT-v0"` instead of the `lerobot/pusht` instruction ("Push the T-shaped block onto
the T-shaped target.").

## Reproduce
```bash
lerobot-eval --policy.path=AleksanderWojsz/smolvla_aloha_sim --env.type=aloha \
  --env.task=AlohaTransferCube-v0 --eval.n_episodes=50 --eval.batch_size=10 \
  --eval.use_async_envs=false --policy.device=mps --seed=1000 --output_dir=out
cat out/task_descriptions.json   # {"AlohaTransferCube-v0_0": "AlohaTransferCube-v0"}
```

## Observed vs expected
| Instruction sent | Success (50 episodes, seeds 1000–1049) | Episodes touching the cube |
|---|---|---|
| `"AlohaTransferCube-v0"` (current) | 0/50, reward 0 in every episode | 0 |
| Dataset instruction from `lerobot/aloha_sim_transfer_cube_human` `meta/tasks.parquet` | 3/50 (6%, 95% CI 2–16%) | 32 |

The same rollout loop gives identical per-episode results for a non-language policy (ACT, 38/50
in both), so the difference is the instruction alone.

## Suggested fix
Give the ALOHA and PushT env configs a default `task_description` equal to the instruction of
their reference datasets, and allow overriding it from the CLI (e.g. `--env.instruction`). At
minimum, warn when a language-conditioned policy receives a `task_description` equal to the gym
id.

## Environment
lerobot 0.7.0, Python 3.12, macOS 26 (M1 Pro, MPS), gym-aloha via `lerobot[aloha]`.

## Related
#4045 is the same class of mismatch for RoboCasa (training task strings vs evaluation prompts). On current `main`, `lerobot_eval.py` still reads the instruction from the env's `task_description`, so this looks unfixed after 0.7.0.
new_candidates.title: ALOHA and PushT sim envs pass the gym id as the language instruction, so VLAs evaluated with `lerobot-eval` score 0

new_candidates.body:
### Ticket Type
🐛 Bug Report (Something isn't working)

### Environment & System Info
- lerobot 0.7.0 (PyPI), Python 3.12, torch 2.15.0, transformers 5.22.2
- macOS 27.2.1, Apple M4 Max, 64 GB
- Checkpoint: `lerobot/MolmoAct2-SO100_101-LeRobot` @ `a4ab68081b84bb0659d96f454edbce6abbe8a1cd`

I ran the 0.7.0 release, not `main`. I did read `configuration_molmoact2.py` on `main` and the fields below are absent there too, so I expect the same failure.

### Description
The `config.json` published in `lerobot/MolmoAct2-SO100_101-LeRobot` cannot be parsed by the current `MolmoAct2Config`. It still contains four fields that no longer exist:

- `enable_lora_vlm`
- `enable_lora_action_expert`
- `train_action_expert_only`
- `model_dtype`

So `PreTrainedConfig.from_pretrained(...)` / `MolmoAct2Policy.from_pretrained(...)` stops before any weights are read.

### Context & Reproduction
```python
from lerobot.configs.policies import PreTrainedConfig
PreTrainedConfig.from_pretrained("lerobot/MolmoAct2-SO100_101-LeRobot")
```

### Relevant logs or stack trace
```
draccus.utils.DecodingError: The fields `enable_lora_vlm`, `enable_lora_action_expert`, `train_action_expert_only`, `model_dtype` are not valid for MolmoAct2Config
```

### Additional Info / Workarounds
Removing the four fields and adding `"train_mode_vlm": "fft"` (the checkpoint stores full weights, `enable_lora_vlm` was `false`) makes it load, and the policy then reproduces recorded actions well (open-loop replay on `Beegbrain/pick_lemon_and_drop_in_bowl`: 2.1° mean abs error vs 11.0° for a hold-position baseline).

Note that the old file had `"model_dtype": "float32"`. After dropping it, the new default `dtype=bfloat16` applies, which changes inference precision compared with what the checkpoint author set. Either re-uploading the config with the current field names (including `dtype`) or a small migration for the old names would fix this.

Small script that applies the workaround: https://github.com/oracle9i88/molmoact2-mac/blob/main/prepare.py
new_candidates.title: MolmoAct2: lerobot/MolmoAct2-SO100_101-LeRobot config.json fails to load (fields removed from MolmoAct2Config)

new_candidates.body:
### Ticket Type
🐛 Bug Report (Something isn't working)

### Environment & System Info
- lerobot 0.7.0 (PyPI), Python 3.12, torch 2.15.0, transformers 5.22.2
- macOS 27.2.1, Apple M4 Max, 64 GB, device `mps`
- Checkpoint: `lerobot/MolmoAct2-SO100_101-LeRobot` (config patched as described in #5374 so that it loads)

Tested on the 0.7.0 release, not `main`.

### Description
MolmoAct2 runs on Apple Silicon through MPS without code changes, and with `dtype=float32` the output is identical to CPU float32. With `dtype=bfloat16` — the default in `MolmoAct2Config` — it runs without any error or warning on MPS but returns clearly different actions for the same input and the same flow-matching start noise.

One 30-step chunk, fixed synthetic input, actions in degrees, compared with CPU float32:

| device / dtype | latency (warm) | max abs diff | mean abs diff |
|---|---|---|---|
| MPS float32 | 0.82 s | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| MPS bfloat16 | 0.80 s | 26.5 | 9.8 |
| CPU float32 | 3.1 s | reference | reference |
| CPU bfloat16 | 15.5 s | 0.30 | 0.06 |

CPU bfloat16 stays within 0.06° of the reference, so this is not ordinary bf16 rounding; something in the bf16 autocast path misbehaves on MPS. I have not isolated which op, and it may well be a PyTorch MPS issue rather than a LeRobot one.

Why I am reporting it here: `_autocast_context` only checks `is_autocast_available("mps")`, which is true, so a Mac user gets the bf16 default and silently wrong joint targets. On a real arm that is hard to tell apart from a weak policy.

### Context & Reproduction
```python
import torch
from lerobot.configs.policies import PreTrainedConfig
from lerobot.policies.molmoact2 import MolmoAct2Policy
from lerobot.policies.molmoact2.processor_molmoact2 import make_molmoact2_pre_post_processors_from_pretrained

def run(device, dtype, ckpt):
    cfg = PreTrainedConfig.from_pretrained(ckpt)
    cfg.device, cfg.dtype, cfg.enable_inference_cuda_graph = device, dtype, False
    policy = MolmoAct2Policy.from_pretrained(ckpt, config=cfg).eval()
    pre, post = make_molmoact2_pre_post_processors_from_pretrained(
        cfg, ckpt, preprocessor_overrides={"device_processor": {"device": device}})
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
    obs = {"observation.images.cam0": torch.rand(3, 224, 224, generator=g),
           "observation.images.cam1": torch.rand(3, 224, 224, generator=g),
           "observation.state": torch.tensor([5.0, -60.0, 70.0, 40.0, 0.0, 20.0]),
           "task": "pick up the red cube and put it in the box"}
    noise = torch.randn(1, cfg.chunk_size, cfg.expected_max_action_dim, generator=g).to(device)
    return post(policy.predict_action_chunk(pre(obs), noise=noise)).float().cpu()

ref = run("cpu", torch.float32, CKPT)
print((run("mps", torch.float32, CKPT) - ref).abs().mean())    # 0.0
print((run("mps", torch.bfloat16, CKPT) - ref).abs().mean())   # ~9.8
```
Complete script with `--save/--ref` comparison: https://github.com/oracle9i88/molmoact2-mac/blob/main/smoke_test.py

### Relevant logs or stack trace
None — that is the problem. No exception, no NaN, no warning.

### Additional Info / Workarounds
Use `dtype=float32` on MPS (20.5 GiB GPU memory for this checkpoint, 0.82 s per chunk on M4 Max).

Suggestion: until the cause is found, raise or warn when `dtype=bfloat16` is combined with an `mps` device, and/or mention in the MolmoAct2 docs that Apple Silicon works with float32 (the docs currently say an NVIDIA GPU is required).
new_candidates.title: MolmoAct2 on MPS: default dtype bfloat16 silently returns wrong actions (float32 matches CPU exactly)
